A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Generative Annotation for ASR Named Entity Correction. All 12 pages, including equations, figures, tables and Appendix A.1–A.5, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original named-entity correction experiments on AISHELL, Word Form Variation and BuzzWord, including commercial-engine results in Appendix Table 6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Tables 2, 3 and 6, together with component comparisons, attention analyses and correction cases.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same speech-based entity retrieval, generative error annotation, entity rejection and text replacement procedure. No architecture, training objective or inference component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same AISHELL training and evaluation data, Word Form Variation subset and BuzzWord test set, including commercial-ASR scenarios. The new availability statement does not change dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Tables 2–3 retain Whisper, PED-NEC, PED+GL, SS+NEC and SS+GL; Table 6 retains the corresponding PED-NEC and SS+GL comparisons for iFlytek and Amazon.

E3.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix A retain the same data construction, sample counts, Whisper configurations, four evaluation metrics, training settings and retrieval thresholds. Baseline tuning and the omission of CED on BuzzWord are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The component comparisons, attention heatmaps, retrieval-threshold analysis, entity-rejection example, training entity-count histogram and correction cases are unchanged, including the appendix analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative examples are unchanged throughout. For example, SS+GL NE-Recall remains 87.31% on AISHELL, 87.47% on BuzzWord, and 81.71% and 80.02% for the iFlytek and Amazon experiments.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6) and their mathematical content remain unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The central claims about generative annotation, handling word-form differences, entity rejection and performance relative to PED-NEC are retained. The abstract's revision concerns resource availability rather than the scientific contribution.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning attention alignment, retrieval noise tolerance and contextual rejection are unchanged. Both versions retain the latency limitation and Appendix A.2's qualification about limited multi-entity training examples.

D1.justification: The abstract changes a promise to release the self-constructed training data and test set into a statement of public availability, adding the github.com/L6-NLP/Generative-Annotation-NEC address. Other implementation and reproducibility details are unchanged; repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list and positioning relative to phonetic edit-distance correction and other ASR correction approaches are unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract's final data-release sentence is revised and the arXiv version/date header changes. The remaining prose, terminology and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: The longer availability statement causes limited text reflow across the first two pages. Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–7 retain their content, structure, captions and placement, with only negligible typesetting differences elsewhere.

improvement.justification: Replacing the abstract's future release promise with a concrete repository address improves data-access and reproducibility documentation. The scientific methods, evidence and limitations remain unchanged, so the improvement is limited. The PDFs establish the documentation gain but do not independently verify the repository's contents.
